sentences.text: Cretorectolobus was an extinct species of carpet shark.
This animal belonged to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes sharks, rays, and skates.
It is classified within the family Orectolobidae.
The species name C. gracilis refers to its teeth, which are described as gracile and narrow.
The genus Cretorectolobus was first described by G.R. Case in 1978.
Cretorectolobus lived from the Hauterivian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 132.6 to 66 million years ago.
The type species, Cretorectolobus olsoni, lived during the Campanian stage in Canada and the United States.
The species Cretorectolobus gracilis lived from the Hauterivian to the Barremian in the Speeton Clay Formation of England.
The species Cretorectolobus robustus lived during the Cenomanian in Canada.
Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Hauterivian-Barremian Speeton Clay Formation in England.
Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Albian Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah and in Kolbay, Kazakhstan.
Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Cenomanian of Saskatchewan, Canada.

Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Campanian Aguja Formation in Mexico, the Dinosaur Park and Judith River Formations in Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Montana, and the Mesaverde Group in Wyoming.
Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in Åsen and Ignaberga, Sweden.
Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Maastrichtian Kemp Clay Formation in Texas and at Bakla Hill in Ukraine.
